units.translation: ⟦1⟧ as above (684), now without mention of the judicial function, although one can see an allusion to it in ⟦2⟧; or does this refer to the prosecutions that Ephialtes had conducted against a number of individual Areopagites ⟦3⟧, Aristot. ⟦4⟧. ⟦5⟧. 25, 2? The character as a supervisory authority emerges especially in ⟦6⟧; for naturally one should not think, with the scholiast on ⟦7⟧, of murdered persons, nor of a night police, but it is spoken figuratively, cf. ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧.
a wakeful guard over those who sleep, for the land
⟦1⟧ equally concrete ⟦2⟧. So according to the poet all this power is an original attribute of the Areopagus, while the democrats recognized originally nothing but the jurisdiction over bloodshed.

707 ⟦1⟧ is a proof that Athena's speech was not as short as Dindorf makes it; for the contrast cf. 571ff. 711-733 voting of the Areopagites, and meanwhile exchange of speeches between the parties in distichomythia, concluded by three verses of the chorus. There are 10 × 2 and then the three verses, without any relation to the number of choreutae; whether in relation to that of the voters? But there must not have been eleven, but an even number, so that equality of votes could result; what the scholiast on 743 says, that there were 51, is a transfer from the number of the Ephetae. O. Müller therefore assumes that one voted after 711, and again one after each speech of the parties, which yields 12; Weil earlier posited the loss of two pairs of verses and did not count the last three verses, with the same final result; Wecklein achieves this still differently and with much greater violence. The exchanges themselves, however, only at the beginning refer to the voting and then become pure altercatio (almost ⟦2⟧) of the parties; I therefore miss the sufficient reason to demand a parallelism between these invectives and the voting.
711 ⟦1⟧ as at 406 ⟦2⟧.. ⟦3⟧, and 720 ⟦4⟧ (which also belongs to the repetitions of this piece mentioned at 696 ff.).
this grievous company of the land
I shall again be a grievous companion to this land
⟦1⟧ threatening precisely through the litotes. Apollo's reply corresponds (to ⟦2⟧): ⟦3⟧ — ⟦4⟧ (= ⟦5⟧, 17, ⟦6⟧). — 715
